decisions.thought: 84% MOVE: hydropump, 15% MOVE: voltswitch, 1% SWITCH: garchomp

Rotom-Wash is faster and resists Flare Blitz, so attacking is poor and costs recoil. Parting Shot lowers Rotom-Wash's Attack and Sp. Atk while bringing in Archaludon, which resists both of Rotom's STAB types. Parting Shot is the best use of this turn.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar's Flare Blitz is resisted by Rotom-Wash since it's Water-type, and Rotom-Wash outspeeds, likely packing Hydro Pump or Volt Switch to threaten back since neither of its typings are weak to Fire.

Thinking about switching to Kingambit instead, since its Dark/Steel typing should resist Rotom-Wash's Electric moves, though I need to double check whether Steel actually resists Electric in this generation.

I'm also weighing whether Incineroar should use Parting Shot here—since Rotom-Wash is faster, it'll get its attack off first, so the sequencing matters for whether the switch happens safely.

Flare Blitz only does half damage to Rotom-Wash, and even with Incineroar's high Attack it likely won't KO, plus the recoil is costly. Switching to Archaludon looks better: its Steel/Dragon typing resists Rotom's Water attacks, and its own Electroshot hits Rotom neutrally, making it a cleaner matchup.

Parting Shot seems like the better play here—it both weakens Rotom's offensive stat and brings in Archaludon safely, accomplishing two things in one move compared to a direct switch.

Garchomp also seems faster here, so Earthquake lands first. Since Garchomp is almost certainly faster, Dracometeor probably won't get off before Earthquake connects. Electroshot also fails outright against a Ground-type, and Flash Cannon is only lukewarm here, so maybe Protect to scout or switching to Kingambit is the safer play against Garchomp's Earthquake.

Dracometeor now would be wasted since Garchomp still moves first and KOs Archaludon before it fires. Protect blocks the Earthquake but gains little tempo, while switching to Kingambit lets it absorb the hit and preserves Archaludon's 47 HP for later. I'm leaning toward switching to Kingambit as the safer play.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Garchomp's Ground typing makes it immune to Electro Shot, so that move is useless here. Draco Meteor would hit Garchomp neutrally since Dragon doesn't resist or get hit super effectively by its own Ground subtype.

Meanwhile Garchomp's Earthquake hits Archaludon's Steel typing for 2x damage, and at only 47 HP Archaludon likely can't survive that given Garchomp's higher speed. I'm also noting Aurora Veil is actually on the opponent's side, which halves damage Garchomp takes, so Draco Meteor's impact against Garchomp's remaining HP would be reduced accordingly.

Garchomp's speed range of 109-169 outpaces Archaludon's 105, so it moves first every turn. Protect only delays the inevitable since Garchomp will just attack again next turn and kill it. The real question is whether going for Dracometeor now could KO Garchomp before it gets another EQ off, even though Archaludon would take the hit first.

Checking the math: Garchomp at 72% HP has roughly 132-155 HP remaining, and Dracometeor through screens only does about 120-141 damage, so it's not a guaranteed kill, and the SpA drop makes it worse if it doesn't finish the job. Given Garchomp outspeeds and EQ kills Archaludon regardless, Protect is the safer play here, buying a turn and hoping the opponent switches.
